Chapter 7: The Power of Absence and Withdrawal
Ever notice how something becomes more valuable the less you see it? Think about rare gems, or even that friend who always seems just a little out of reach. When you use absence on purpose, it can actually boost your influence and make people appreciate you much more.
Here’s the thing: we’re wired to overlook what’s always around. If you’re always available—always jumping into every meeting, call, or request—it’s easy for others to take you for granted. But when you step back at just the right moment, you create a spark of curiosity. People start to wonder, “Where did they go?” or “When will they be back?” That sense of mystery and anticipation makes your presence feel special.
So, how can you put this idea into practice? Well, try limiting your access. Don’t say yes to every meeting or favor. If you’re always in the spotlight, take a purposeful step back and let others miss your input. After a big win, consider withdrawing for a bit—leave people wanting more instead of risking overstaying your welcome. And when you’re offering your skills or resources, do it selectively; don’t spread yourself thin.
Think about a consultant who’s always free—there’s not much excitement in booking time with them. But if they’re in demand, maybe even a little hard to get ahold of? Suddenly, their time feels precious. Clients can’t wait to hear what they have to say.
Absence isn’t just about boosting your value—it’s also a powerful reset button, especially in relationships. When things get tense or emotions run high, stepping back allows everyone some breathing room. Often, when you reconnect, there’s more respect, and a fresh perspective.
Of course, it’s all about balance. Pulling away too much? You risk being forgotten or replaced. The trick is to stay present enough to matter, but absent enough to be missed.
So, what’s the real takeaway here? The power of absence and withdrawal is about creating space—for appreciation, reflection, and influence. When used thoughtfully, it’s a subtle but highly effective way to shape how others see you, and to maintain real control over your impact.
